price_per_million.source: openrouter.ai/models, confirmed via preflight 2026-11-11; thinking tokens billed as output

methodological_questions: What does 'preceding' mean: the same possession, or the immediately prior possession by the same team? Can the derived possession records express it?
Is a PNR possession that follows a drive different in ways that confound PPP (shot clock, lineup, team quality, ball handler)?
Do play-type labels and foul-ending shares bias PNR or DRIVE PPP?
Is there enough exposure to detect a PPP effect of about 0.05-0.10, and does it hold across seasons and playoffs?
Is a universal claim ('any' drive) testable, or only an average effect with heterogeneity?

historical_evidence.finding: After the opponent runs play type X, the next offensive play type Y scores above Y's unconditional H2 baseline. Every play type shows a defensive aftershock (CUT +0.119, DRIVE +0.123, PNR +0.127 in all games). Limited by small sample. The record concerns opponent-play-type to own-next-play-type sequences, not a teammate drive before a PNR.

Descriptive player and teammate X->Y sequential premiums over Y's baseline. Same-player L. Doncic DRIVE->PNR +0.309 (n=53). D. Bane DRIVE->PNR -0.324 (n=70, t=-2.7). Most cells are described as DIRECT (text cut). Failure mechanism recorded as unclear. Limited by small sample and label/classification error.
Team-level DRIVE PPP is 1.198 in the regular season vs 0.912 in the playoffs (-0.286). PNR PPP is -0.173 lower in the playoffs. Based on 25 teams, a minimum of 30 possessions per cell, and no CIs.

Play-type labeling audit. OTHER PPP is inflated by 36% foul endings. DRIVE sits 12pp below the foul benchmark (foul leakage). PNR shows a 22% foul rate. initiation_type maps only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) to a real play type.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating raw play-type PPP differences as real efficiency, and using initiation_type to label play types
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact: foul-ending leakage inflates or deflates PPP by play type, and initiation_type maps only 0.7% of possessions.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading individual player and teammate X->Y sequence cells as effects
failed_approaches.why: Recorded limits are small sample and label/classification error. Cells are n of about 30-70, signs are mixed (Doncic +0.309 vs Bane -0.324), and the failure mechanism is recorded as unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Pooling regular-season and playoff PPP by play type
failed_approaches.why: Playoff PPP differs sharply from the regular season (DRIVE -0.286, PNR -0.173). The record has no CIs and a minimum of only 30 possessions per cell.

evidence_establishes: Sequential cells (DRIVE->PNR) can be built from the derived records, and the record gives examples with n of about 50-70 per player.
Player-level DRIVE->PNR premiums are heterogeneous in sign (FAM:SF40 records Doncic +0.309 and Bane -0.324), so a universal 'any drive raises PNR PPP' is not supported by what was retrieved.
Play-type PPP is contaminated by foul-ending and labeling artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-025), and PNR PPP differs between the regular season and playoffs (FAM:SF-APPS-011).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests a league-wide, adjusted effect of a teammate drive on subsequent PNR PPP.
They do not show whether the derived records capture within-possession sequences or only consecutive-possession pairs.
They do not show that DRIVE->PNR premiums survive controls for lineup, ball handler, shot clock or foul-ending share.
The FAM:SF40 per-cell results are not hypothesis tests, and their text is truncated.
own_inferences: 'Any' is a universal claim and cannot be confirmed by a statistical test. The testable version is an average effect plus a heterogeneity description.
Raw DRIVE->PNR cells are likely confounded: a drive before a PNR marks possession and player context (for example star ball handlers or late-clock situations), not just a causal action.
A PNR possession that follows a drive may also be a different sample of PNRs (longer possessions, different defensive state).
Foul-ending contamination of PNR (22% foul rate) could differ between preceded and non-preceded PNRs and fake or mask an effect.
A pooled effect, if one exists, is probably small (about 0.0-0.1 PPP), and is detectable only with pooled league-wide data, not per-player cells.
uncertainties: Whether 'preceding' is coded within the same possession or across consecutive possessions in the derived records.
The exact PNR and DRIVE labeling rules and how many PNRs are preceded by a teammate drive (exposure).
The full text of FAM:SF40 and FAM:SF07 was cut; read_family was not called.
Whether the 2025-26 playoffs data (complete from 2026-06-21) will be available; it is partial at the question date.
Whether the label-quality issue in FAM:SF-CHT-025 has been fixed in the current graph build.

historical_effect.explanation: The history shifted the decision from a simple proceed to proceed_with_changes. It showed that raw sequence cells are small-n and sign-heterogeneous, and that PPP by play type carries foul-ending labeling artifacts and regular-season/playoff drift. The universal claim has to be replaced by an adjusted average effect, with foul-ending handling and a separate playoff analysis.

blocking_constraints.text: If the derived records cannot identify a teammate drive within the same possession and before the PNR, the question cannot be tested as posed.
Without matching or adjustment for ball handler, lineup, opponent and clock, any difference is not attributable to the drive.

prior_work.summary: Only descriptive DRIVE->PNR cells exist (FAM:SF40, not a hypothesis test, small n, mixed signs). Labeling and foul artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-025) and playoff drift (FAM:SF-APPS-011) are documented. No retrieved record tests an adjusted pooled effect of a teammate drive on PNR PPP.

risks.text: Drive-preceded PNRs differ by ball handler, lineup, opponent, score and clock. Adjust with fixed effects and matching.
Derived play-type labels are imperfect (initiation_type maps 0.7% in FAM:SF-CHT-025), and 'preceding' is ambiguous in the possession records.

PNR, DRIVE and foul endings are derived from play-by-play outcomes. A drive that draws a foul or ends a possession can alter later labeling and PPP. Use outcome-independent labels and report with and without foul-ending possessions.
Per-player cells are n of about 30-70 (FAM:SF40), too small. Only the pooled analysis is adequately powered.
The share of PNRs preceded by a teammate drive within a short window may be small. Check counts before analysis.
Playoff PPP differs from the regular season (FAM:SF-APPS-011). Analyze regular season and playoffs separately and check season stability.
Heterogeneity analyses by player, team and season multiply comparisons. Pre-specify one primary test.
Conditioning on later possession events, such as total possession length, would leak outcome information. Condition only on pre-PNR information.
Selecting top players or cells by premium (as in the FAM:SF40 top-cell lists) produces regression to the mean. Do not select by outcome.

design.estimand: Average difference in PNR PPP (points per possession, including free throws, with a sensitivity analysis excluding foul-ending possessions) between PNR possessions preceded by a teammate DRIVE (a non-PNR-initiator, within a pre-specified window such as the same possession and at most 8 seconds before the screen) and matched PNR possessions with no preceding drive. The universal claim 'any drive' is not tested; instead report the pooled average effect and the share of ball-handler/driver cells with positive effects.
design.sample: 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular seasons (the 2025-26 regular season is complete). Playoffs analyzed separately as a confirmatory hold-out. The 2025-26 playoffs are included only if the complete version is frozen; otherwise excluded. Exclude garbage time and possessions where the drive or PNR label is ambiguous.
design.power: With SD of about 1.15 PPP and a target effect of 0.08, about 3,200 per group gives 80% power at two-sided alpha 0.05, before cluster adjustment. Verify the exposed count first. If fewer than about 2,000 preceded PNRs are available, declare the test underpowered rather than a null.
design.controls: Fixed effects for the PNR ball handler, offense and defense team-season, and lineup. Covariates are score margin, period, shot clock or time into possession at the screen, and the foul-ending share. Coarsened matching on those covariates. Report both the matched and the regression estimates.
design.falsification: Placebo: replace the preceding teammate drive with a preceding non-drive action (for example a spot-up or an off-ball cut) and with a drive that occurs after the PNR, and expect no effect. Permutation of the preceded label within ball handler and game. Label-audit on a manually checked sample of 200 sequences.
design.multiplicity: One primary test, the pooled adjusted effect. Secondary tests by season, playoffs vs regular season, and foul-excluded sensitivity are labeled exploratory, with Holm correction across the secondary set.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the adjusted pooled effect is at least +0.05 PPP with 95% CI lower bound above 0, the sign is the same in at least 3 of 4 seasons, and the placebo effects are indistinguishable from 0. Rejected if the 95% CI lies within +/-0.04 with at least 80% power. Artifact if the effect disappears when foul endings are excluded or the placebo is also significant. Otherwise uncertain. 'Any' is never claimed.
design.data_version: Freeze the graph-database build and per-game files as of 2026-06-14 (the 2025-26 regular season complete, the playoffs partial). Record the build hash, the derived-label code version and the date of any later playoff data. The playoff confirmation is run only after the 2025-26 playoffs complete on 2026-06-21.

research_concepts: sequence of actions within a possession
methodological_questions: Does a preceding teammate drive causally raise PNR PPP or is it confounded by possession context and team/player quality?
How reliable is the derived play-type label and the definition of 'preceding' drive in play-by-play data?
Is there enough exposure and sample size to detect an effect on PPP, and are there outcome-derived label or lookahead risks?
Can the effect be tested with matched or within-player comparisons and placebo controls?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether follow-up tool calls are worth it, but I think I can finish directly. A read_family on SF40 might help, but the budget allows it either way, so I'll stay focused. The retrieval result reports n_results as 4 and lists 4, so that's consistent.

I'm checking the teammate DRIVE-before-PNR cells, which look mixed: Bane's comes out negative and Doncic's positive, on small samples, so that isn't a real test of the claim. The SF07 and SF-APPS-011 results don't speak to a teammate drive preceding the play, and the CHT-025 labeling issue, where DRIVE foul leakage inflates PNR fouls, needs care too.

I'm settling on the data-version question: the 2025-26 playoff data isn't complete until after the question date, so I'll use the completed regular season and hold the playoffs out. I'm also weighing whether "preceding" means earlier in the same possession or in a prior possession, since the sequence data seems to be across consecutive possessions. Then I'll assign rough probabilities to the outcomes, with about 0.4 odds that the claim is testable at all, and lean toward proceeding with a reformulated version.

I'm working out the power for this test: at 80% power with a two-sided α of .05, detecting a 0.10 PPP difference with a per-possession SD near 1.15 needs roughly 2,000 possessions per group, which seems feasible if pooled across several seasons. I'll cluster the standard errors by team-game and make the decision rule explicit before looking at results.

I'm settling the decision rule: the claim gets reframed as an average effect, and it counts as supported only if the adjusted pooled difference is at least +0.05 PPP with a positive lower confidence bound and consistent sign across most seasons. I'll report how the effect varies across drivers rather than asserting the universal "any" version, and I'll write up the result as JSON.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether follow-up tool calls are worth it, but I think I can finish directly. A read_family on SF40 might help, but the budget allows it either way, so I'll stay focused. The retrieval result reports n_results as 4 and lists 4, so that's consistent.

I'm checking the teammate DRIVE-before-PNR cells, which look mixed: Bane's comes out negative and Doncic's positive, on small samples, so that isn't a real test of the claim. The SF07 and SF-APPS-011 results don't speak to a teammate drive preceding the play, and the CHT-025 labeling issue, where DRIVE foul leakage inflates PNR fouls, needs care too.

I'm settling on the data-version question: the 2025-26 playoff data isn't complete until after the question date, so I'll use the completed regular season and hold the playoffs out. I'm also weighing whether "preceding" means earlier in the same possession or in a prior possession, since the sequence data seems to be across consecutive possessions. Then I'll assign rough probabilities to the outcomes, with about 0.4 odds that the claim is testable at all, and lean toward proceeding with a reformulated version.

I'm working out the power for this test: at 80% power with a two-sided α of .05, detecting a 0.10 PPP difference with a per-possession SD near 1.15 needs roughly 2,000 possessions per group, which seems feasible if pooled across several seasons. I'll cluster the standard errors by team-game and make the decision rule explicit before looking at results.

I'm settling the decision rule: the claim gets reframed as an average effect, and it counts as supported only if the adjusted pooled difference is at least +0.05 PPP with a positive lower confidence bound and consistent sign across most seasons. I'll report how the effect varies across drivers rather than asserting the universal "any" version, and I'll write up the result as JSON.
